gap: No result ChatGPT got states that Jackery measures its cycle life to a different end point than the others: the Explorer 300D and the new Explorer 300 are rated for '4,000+ cycles to 70% capacity', while BLUETTI rates the Elite 30 V2 at 'over 3,000 cycles' with no end point given, so the bigger cycle number does not mean a longer life.
standout_why: I compared the cited Gadgeteer C300 DC review, the cited manuals.plus C300 DC guide (its PDF text would not extract) and the top-14 result Amphourly 'Best Small Portable Power Stations Under 500Wh'. Gadgeteer already gives the C300 DC's 300 W total USB limit and its port-sharing table, but no cycle rating. Amphourly gives an 80% end point for the RIVER 3 and 300 Plus and no end point for the Elite 30 V2. It never mentions 70% and publishes no cycle rating for the C300. So the 70%-versus-80% difference is new, but it matters over years of use, not on one weekend.
decides: This confirms the pick rather than changing it. Cycle life does not decide whether a unit gets through a laptop weekend, so the footnote only stops a shopper from reading the 300D's '4,000 cycles' as better than '3,000 to 80%'. The facts that matter more for this question are these. The 300D's third USB-C port is only 65 W (C1 and C2 are 140 W), which fills in the port detail ChatGPT told shoppers to 'verify'. Jackery's store says the Explorer 300 v2 is sold out and points to the new Explorer 300 (292 Wh, 7.5 lb, 100 W USB-C), even though ChatGPT showed the v2 as a card. BLUETTI says the Elite 30 V2 has 'only 4.5W standby' but does not say in which mode. If that draw ran all weekend it would be 216 Wh, so I would not put it on the page until the mode is sourced. The Anker C300 DC or Jackery 300D is still the lightest way to get 100 W or more over USB-C.

The manuals.plus PDF would not extract to text, and a local extraction needed approval. A search snippet citing Renewable Outdoors gave '3000 cycles to 80%', but that page returned HTTP 429 so I could not open it.

EcoFlow TRAIL 300 DC weight, USB-C port ratings, cycle life and end point, and price: us.ecoflow.com returned HTTP 429 on every attempt. The storecheck search only showed the series listing ('TRAIL Series DC', from $109.00, compare-at $250.00) and did not break out the 300 DC variant. The ecoflow.com/us spec URLs returned 404, and the Renewable Outdoors page returned 429.
EcoFlow RIVER 3 cycle-life end point from EcoFlow: the maker page returned 404. Only Amphourly, a rival page, states 3,000 cycles to 80%.
Which mode BLUETTI's 4.5 W Elite 30 V2 standby figure refers to (AC on, DC on or screen-off idle): the store listing does not say, and the BLUETTI product page fetch failed with too many redirects.

Measured usable USB-C Wh for the Jackery 300D, Anker C300 DC, EcoFlow TRAIL 300 DC and BLUETTI Elite 30 V2: I found no named reviewer's measurement within budget. Amphourly's figures are 85%-of-rated estimates, not measurements.
